Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L06_GuidedPractice_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which choice best shows relevant evidence?

answer.text: A. The speaker likes the color blue

feedback.text: This detail is unrelated to speech revision.

answer.text: B. Some presentations happen on Fridays

feedback.text: This does not support a claim about improving speeches.

answer.text: C. A peer can identify an unclear transition during practice

feedback.text: Correct. This evidence directly supports the value of peer rehearsal.

answer.text: D. The classroom has chairs

feedback.text: This observation is not relevant evidence for the claim.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L06_GuidedPractice_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which choice best shows evidence explanation?

answer.text: A. This evidence matters because feedback helps the speaker revise before presenting

feedback.text: Correct. This explains how the evidence supports the reasoning.

answer.text: B. This evidence is evidence

feedback.text: This repeats the label and does not explain the connection.

answer.text: C. The claim is good because it is good

feedback.text: This repeats an opinion instead of explaining support.

answer.text: D. Everyone should agree immediately

feedback.text: Persuasion needs reasoning, not pressure.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L06_GuidedPractice_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.LST.04

Which choice best shows credible support?

answer.text: A. A random online comment proves all school rules

feedback.text: A random comment is not reliable enough for credible support.

answer.text: B. A rumor from one student is always enough

feedback.text: A rumor is not strong evidence for a persuasive speech.

answer.text: C. A guess can replace evidence

feedback.text: A guess does not justify reasoning.

answer.text: D. A school handbook is reliable evidence for a speech about school rules

feedback.text: Correct. The handbook is connected to the topic and likely trustworthy.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L06_GuidedPractice_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.RES.02

Which choice best shows justifying reasoning?

answer.text: A. The example is long, so it must be useful

feedback.text: Length does not prove relevance or usefulness.

answer.text: B. The example justifies the reason by showing how the problem can be fixed

feedback.text: Correct. It explains why the evidence proves the reasoning.

answer.text: C. The reason needs no support

feedback.text: Reasoning is stronger when evidence supports it.

answer.text: D. The audience can figure it out alone

feedback.text: A speaker should explain the connection for the audience.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: SPEECH_U03_L06_GuidedPractice_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.SPEECH.COM.01

Which choice best shows weak evidence use?

answer.text: A. Explaining how a fact supports the claim

feedback.text: This is strong evidence use, not weak evidence use.

answer.text: B. Choosing evidence that directly fits the claim

feedback.text: Relevant evidence strengthens the speech.

answer.text: C. Dropping a fact into the speech without explaining it

feedback.text: Correct. Evidence needs explanation to support reasoning.

answer.text: D. Connecting the example to the rebuttal

feedback.text: This helps the audience understand the rebuttal.
